title: Case Report: Multimodal treatment of cervical intramedullary spinal cord metastasis from gastric adenocarcinoma.
summary: Intramedullary spinal cord metastasis (ISCM) from gastric adenocarcinoma is extremely rare, and treatment is not standardized. summary: To enable early detection and treatment of Alzheimer's disease, a better understanding of the heterogeneous disease progression is needed. Longitudinal MRI data has been utilized by previous studies to uncover patterns of brain atrophy. title: Aesthetic preference for the visual appearance of modern decorative cabinets in young adults: An ERP study.
summary: This study investigated the neural processing underlying aesthetic preferences for the visual appearance of modern decorative cabinets and examined whether cabinets associated with different preference levels elicited distinct event-related potential (ERP) responses. Electroencephalography (EEG) was recorded from 31 young adults while they viewed modern decorative cabinet images and standardized affective pictures from the Chinese Affective Picture System (CAPS), which served as an affective reference set. title: Systemic therapy and radiotherapy for small-cell lung cancer brain metastases.
summary: Brain metastases are a defining biological feature of small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) and a persistent blind spot in therapeutic development. Chemo-immunotherapy has improved survival in extensive-stage SCLC, and durvalumab consolidation has changed care for limited-stage disease, but these advances do not establish intracranial efficacy. Patients with active or symptomatic brain metastases remain under-represented in pivotal trials; brain imaging is inconsistent; and prophylactic cranial irradiation, previous radiotherapy and corticosteroid exposure confound interpretation. title: Success rate of MRI scanning during natural sleep for younger autistic and typically developing toddlers.
summary: Toddlerhood represents a critical period of brain development in autism, yet there is limited magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) data for children ages 1-3 years. These ages are difficult to scan without sedation because toddlers tend to have difficulty falling asleep in noisy, unfamiliar environments and following instructions to stay still. While some studies have successfully scanned typically-developing toddlers without sedation, fewer have scanned autistic toddlers. The few with high success rates (>90%) are not easily replicated (e.g., flexible scan durations). title: TSPO-SPECT imaging as a possible biomarker of disease progression in patients with Multiple Sclerosis: A Danish pilot study.
summary: Reliable biomarkers for disease progression in multiple sclerosis (MS) are lacking. Translocator protein (TSPO) expression is increased in microglia and other cell types during neuroinflammation, and TSPO imaging is widely used as an in vivo marker of neuroinflammatory processes. title: Association of autoimmune disease with white matter hyperintensity and recurrent ischemic stroke in young adults with acute ischemic stroke.
summary: Ischemic stroke in young adults is etiologically heterogeneous, and non-traditional factors such as autoimmune disease may play an important role. This study evaluated the association of autoimmune disease with moderate-to-severe white matter hyperintensity (WMH) and recurrent ischemic stroke in patients younger than 50 years with acute ischemic stroke. title: Volume of the mammillary bodies and cognitive trajectories in preclinical Alzheimer's disease.
summary: As part of the Papez circuit, the mammillary bodies (MB) play a key role in episodic memory, but their contribution to cognitive changes in preclinical Alzheimer's disease (AD) remains underexplored. Here, we investigated the associations between MB volume and cognitive decline in cognitively unimpaired older individuals, and whether these associations differed by Aβ status. title: Resting-state network dysconnectivity in schizophrenia: Findings from within- and between-network connectivity analyses.
summary: Schizophrenia is a severe psychiatric disorder associated with functional dysconnectivity within and between large-scale brain networks, though existing literature exhibits significant variability. This study aims to independently replicate and validate these brain disruptions using resting-state fMRI data from 50 patients with schizophrenia and 121 healthy controls. title: A report-supervised EEG-language foundation model enables broad, interactive clinical interpretation
summary: Medical AI for complex signals such as electroencephalography (EEG) relies on costly expert annotations and predefined diagnostic labels that fail to capture the richness and nuance of clinical interpretation. Whether models trained on routine clinical reports can overcome these limitations while matching expert-supervised performance remains unclear. We introduce EEG Copilot, a biosignal-language foundation model trained on routine EEG-report pairs without dedicated task-specific expert annotations.
